description: Open CCAM shows how often each medical and surgical procedure is performed in every French hospital doing acute medicine, surgery and obstetrics, and how long the patients concerned stay. It is published by ATIH, the national agency that manages the hospital discharge database (PMSI), on its ScanSanté statistics site. Coverage is all public and private establishments reporting to the PMSI for acute care, with one data file per level: establishment, region and France. For each procedure code of the French classification of medical procedures (CCAM), the files give the number of stays, sessions and ambulatory stays in which it was performed, the mean length of those stays and the number of times it was carried out. The files are free and available to download from the ScanSanté open data page. Caveats: counts below eleven are masked, with extra cells suppressed so they cannot be deduced, procedure codes need the CCAM nomenclature to interpret, and ScanSanté is moving to a new platform so addresses may change. Simulation uses: estimating operating theatre and procedure demand by hospital, and setting length-of-stay parameters for surgical capacity and patient flow models. Related records: the DREES SAE (data-drees-sae-hospital-annual-statistics) gives the beds and equipment of the same establishments, and the US HCUP databases (data-ahrq-hcup-hospital-utilization-databases) are a comparable discharge source.
